sentences.l: Then must the servants the king’s-son a sleeping-draught in give, and then lays she herself on the sill and whimpers the whole night,
sentences.i: Then the servants had to give the king’s son a sleeping-draught, and she lay down on the threshold and whimpered the whole night through,
sentences.n: Schlopdrunk = ‘Schlaftrunk’; ingiewen = ‘eingeben’, to administer. günselt is glossed by the Grimms, (winselt). heile = ‘ganze’. He lay on that same kind of threshold for her three nights at the beginning; now she lies on his.

sentences.t: se hädde den Wall für ün afhoggen loten, se hädde de Dieck fur ün utschloen, se hädde dat Schlott für ün bugget,
sentences.l: she had the wood for him hewn down let, she had the pond for him dug out, she had the castle for him built,
sentences.i: she had had the wood cut down for him, she had had the pond dug out for him, she had had the castle built for him,
sentences.n: Her whole lament is reported speech, marked only by the subjunctive hädde. für and fur are one word, ‘für’, spelled two ways inside a single sentence.

sentences.t: se hädde ünne ton Dörenbusk macket, dann wier tor Kerke un tolest tom Dieck, un he hädde se so geschwinne vergeten.
sentences.l: she had him into the thorn-bush made, then again into the church and at last into the pond, and he had her so quickly forgotten.
sentences.i: she had turned him into the thorn-bush, then into the church, and at last into the pond — and he had forgotten her so quickly.
sentences.n: ton = ‘zum’, into the — not ‘Ton’, a sound. geschwinne = ‘geschwind’, quickly. The three transformations are counted off like a list of debts.

sentences.t: De Künigssuhn hadde nicks davon hört, de Bedeinten awerst würen upwacket un hadden tolustert un hadden nie wust wat et sull bedüen.
sentences.l: The king’s-son had nothing of it heard, the servants however were woken and had listened in and had not known what it should mean.
sentences.i: The king’s son had heard nothing of it, but the servants had woken and listened, and had not known what it might mean.
sentences.n: tolustert = ‘zugelauscht’, listened in; wust here is ‘gewusst’, known — not ‘willst’; bedüen = ‘bedeuten’; nie is ‘nicht’ again.

sentences.t: Den anneren Morgen, ase se upstohen würen, do trock de Brut dat Kleid an, un fort mit den Brümen nah der Kerke.
sentences.l: The next morning, when they got up were, then drew the bride the dress on, and off with the bridegroom to the church.
sentences.i: The next morning, when they had got up, the bride put the dress on, and off she went with the bridegroom to the church.
sentences.n: upstohen = ‘aufgestanden’; trock … an = ‘zog … an’. fort with no verb at all — “and off to the church” — is exactly the ellipsis English uses.

sentences.t: Unnerdes macket dat wackere Mäken de tweide Wallnutt up, un do is nau en schöner Kleid inne,
sentences.l: Meanwhile opens the fair girl the second walnut up, and there is a still finer dress inside,
sentences.i: Meanwhile the fair girl opened the second walnut, and there was a still finer dress inside,
sentences.n: nau here is ‘noch’ in its comparative use, a still finer dress. Wallnutt = ‘Walnuss’.

sentences.t: dat thüt et wier an un geit domie in de Kerke gigen den Altor stohen, do geit et dann ewen wie dat vürge mol.
sentences.l: that puts it on again and goes with it into the church up to the altar to stand, then goes it then just as the previous time.
sentences.i: she put it on again and went in it into the church to stand before the altar, and then it went just as it had the time before.
sentences.n: thüt = ‘zieht’ — another spelling of the verb written trecket a few lines back. ewen = ‘eben’, just; vürge = ‘vorige’, previous.

sentences.t: Un dat Mäken liegt wier en Nacht für den Süll, de nah des Künigsuhns Stobe geit,
sentences.l: And the girl lies again one night before the sill, which to the king’s-son’s chamber goes,
sentences.i: And the girl lay another night before the threshold that leads to the king’s son’s chamber,
sentences.n: Stobe = ‘Stube’, room. Künigsuhns here, Künigssuhns elsewhere — the 1857 text keeps both spellings.

sentences.t: un de Bedeinten süllt ün wier en Schlopdrunk ingiewen; de Bedeinten kummet awerst un giewet ünne wat to wacken, domie legt he sik to Bedde:
sentences.l: and the servants shall him again a sleeping-draught in give; the servants come however and give him something to stay awake, with that lays he himself to bed:
sentences.i: and the servants were to give him a sleeping-draught again; but the servants came and gave him something to keep him awake, and with that he went to bed:
sentences.n: süllt = ‘sollt, sollen’; wat to wacken = ‘was zum Wachen’, something for staying awake. The servants act on their own: they heard the lament the night before, and this is their answer to it.

sentences.t: un de Müllersmaged fur den Dörsüll günselt wier so viel un segd wat se dohen hädde.
sentences.l: and the miller’s-maid before the door-sill whimpers again so much and says what she done had.
sentences.i: and the miller’s maid before the threshold whimpered again as before, and told what she had done.
sentences.n: Müllersmaged = ‘Müllersmagd’, the miller’s maidservant — the tale calls her that now, not king’s daughter. fur = ‘vor’.

sentences.t: Dat hört olle de Künigssuhn un werd gans bedröwet, un et föllt ünne olle wier bie wat vergangen was.
sentences.l: That hears all the king’s-son and becomes quite grieved, and it falls him all again in what passed was.
sentences.i: The king’s son heard it all and was utterly grieved, and it all came back to him, everything that had happened.
sentences.n: bifallen is ‘einfallen’ in the sense of coming back to mind: et föllt ünne … bie = ‘es fällt ihm … bei’, it occurs to him. vergangen was = ‘vergangen war’, had gone by.

sentences.t: Do will he nah ehr gohen, awerst sine Moder hadde de Dör toschlotten.
sentences.l: Then wants he to her to go, but his mother had the door locked.
sentences.i: He wanted to go to her, but his mother had locked the door.
sentences.n: Dör here is ‘Tür’, door — the same spelling means ‘durch’, through, elsewhere in Low German, and only the sentence decides it. toschlotten = ‘zugeschlossen’.

sentences.t: Den annern Morgen awerst gieng he gliek to siner Leiwesten un vertellte ehr olles, wie et mit ünne togangen wür,
sentences.l: The next morning however went he at once to his dearest and told her everything, how it with him gone on had,
sentences.i: But the next morning he went straight to his dearest and told her everything, how it had gone with him,
sentences.n: togangen = ‘zugegangen’, come about; siner Leiwesten = ‘seiner Liebsten’; vertellte = ‘erzählte’.

sentences.t: un se mögte ünne doch nig beuse sin dat he se so lange vergetten hädde.
sentences.l: and she might him after all not angry be that he her so long forgotten had.
sentences.i: and she should not be angry with him, after all, that he had forgotten her so long.
sentences.n: beuse sin = ‘böse sein’, to be angry — sin here is the infinitive ‘sein’, not the possessive ‘sein’ it was in the tale’s first line. vergetten = ‘vergessen’.

sentences.t: Do macket de Künigsdochter de dridde Wallnutt up, do is nau en viel wackerer Kleid inne:
sentences.l: Then opens the king’s-daughter the third walnut up, there is a still much finer dress inside:
sentences.i: Then the king’s daughter opened the third walnut, and there was a still much finer dress inside:
sentences.n: dridde = ‘dritte’. She is de Künigsdochter again from this line on — the tale gives her the title back the moment he remembers her.

sentences.t: dat trecket sie an un fört mit ehrem Brünen nah de Kerke, un do keimen so viele Kinner, de geiwen ünne Blomen un hellen ünne bunte Bänner fur de Föte,
sentences.l: that puts she on and goes with her bridegroom to the church, and there came so many children, who gave them flowers and held them bright ribbons before the feet,
sentences.i: she put it on and went with her bridegroom to the church, and so many children came, who gave them flowers and held bright ribbons before their feet,
sentences.n: fört = ‘fährt’, goes, drives. Brünen is a third spelling of Brüme, ‘Bräutigam’. hellen is ‘hielten’, held — not ‘hell’, bright. Bänner = ‘Bänder’; Föte = ‘Füße’. ünne does duty here for ‘ihnen’, them — everywhere else in the tale it is ‘ihm’. Barring a bridal couple’s way with ribbons was a real wedding custom: the road opens when the couple pays a forfeit.

sentences.t: un se leiten sik insegnen un hellen ene lustige Hochtied; awerst de falske Moder un Brut mosten weg.
sentences.l: and they let themselves be blessed and held a merry wedding; but the false mother and bride had to go.
sentences.i: and they let themselves be married, and held a merry wedding; but the false mother and bride had to go.
sentences.n: leiten is ‘ließen’, let — not ‘leiten’, to lead. Hochtied = ‘Hochzeit’; falske = ‘falsche’. The tale disposes of both women in five words and does not say where they went.

sentences.t: Un we dat lest vertellt het, den is de Mund noch wärm.
sentences.l: And who that last told has, to him is the mouth still warm.
sentences.i: And whoever told this last, his mouth is still warm.
sentences.n: we = ‘wer’, whoever; lest = ‘zuletzt’; wärm = ‘warm’. This is a closing tag of the kind tellers used to sign off with — the tale has only just left somebody’s mouth. Several of the Low German tales in the collection end on such a formula.

glossary.anne: Low German: daran, an — on it, at it; also the separable particle an (‘anne keimen’ = ankamen)
glossary.antworte: Low German: antworte — answer (antworten, imperative sg.)
glossary.berge: Low German: dem Berge — mountain (dat. sg. of Berg)
glossary.bergen: Low German: bergen — to save or help oneself (‘sik nig to bergen weten’ = sich nicht zu helfen wissen; the Grimms gloss it (helfen))
glossary.bold: Low German: bald — soon; here nearly, all but
glossary.brocht: Low German: gebracht — brought (bringen, past participle without ge-)
glossary.d: d. i. — das ist, that is (the Grimms’ own abbreviation inside their bracketed gloss)
glossary.den: Low German: den, dem — the (acc. sg. masc.; also dat. sg., where High German has dem: ‘in den Holte’ = in dem Holze)
glossary.der: Low German: der, die — the (dat. sg. fem.); who, which; also ‘da(r)’, there (‘do stund der’ = da stand)
glossary.di: Low German: dir, dich — you (dat./acc. of du)
glossary.die: Low German: dir, dich — you (dat./acc. of du); also ‘die’, the (def. art.)
glossary.dören: Low German: der Dorn — thorn (also pl., Dornen)
glossary.eins: Low German: eins — one, one thing (‘nau eins dohen’ = noch eins tun, to do one thing more)
glossary.enne: Low German: das Ende — end (‘to Enne’ = zu Ende, at an end)
glossary.frau: Low German: froh — glad (‘so frau ase en Vugel’ = so froh wie ein Vogel)
glossary.frigget: Low German: freit; gefreit — weds, marries; married (frigen = freien, 3rd sg. and past participle)
glossary.froget: Low German: fragt, gefragt — asks, asked (fragen)
glossary.föllt: Low German: fällt — falls (fallen, 3rd sg.; ‘et föllt ünne bie’ = es fällt ihm bei, it comes back to him)
glossary.für: Low German: vor; für — before, in front of; for (Low German för covers both)
glossary.gans: Low German: ganz — quite, wholly, entirely
glossary.geschirr: Low German: das Geschirr — gear, tools, tackle
glossary.gesichte: Low German: dem Gesicht — sight (‘ut den Gesichte verloren’ = aus dem Gesicht verloren, lost from sight)
glossary.gienge: gehen — ginge, would go (3rd sg. subjunctive); also gingen, went (3rd pl. past; 1857 spelling)
glossary.hellen: Low German: hielten — held (holen = halten, 3rd pl. past)
glossary.hewen: Low German: haben — to have (hebben = haben, infinitive; ‘tor Frugge hewen’ = zur Frau haben)
glossary.holt: Low German: das Holz — wood, forest
glossary.holte: Low German: dem Holze — wood, forest (dat.)
glossary.hät: Low German: haben — have (hebben = haben, 1st pl.; ‘wie hät dohen’ = wir haben getan)
glossary.hört: Low German: hört; gehört — hears; heard (hören)
glossary.i: d. i. — das ist, that is (the i of the Grimms’ abbreviation d. i.)
glossary.inne: Low German: darin, drinnen — in it, inside; also the particle of inschlopen (= einschlafen)
glossary.keimen: Low German: kamen — came (kummen = kommen, 3rd pl. past)
glossary.kiel: Low German: der Keil — wedge, for splitting wood
glossary.kregen: Low German: gekriegt, bekommen — got (kriegen, past participle)
glossary.kämen: Low German: kamen — came (kummen = kommen, 3rd pl. past)
glossary.könnt: Low German: gekonnt — been able (können, past participle)
glossary.legt: Low German: legt; liegt — lays, puts; lies (leggen = legen and liggen = liegen fall together in this spelling)
glossary.leiten: Low German: ließen — let (loten = lassen, 3rd pl. past)
glossary.lett: Low German: läßt — lets, allows (loten = lassen, 3rd sg.)
glossary.loten: Low German: lassen — to let; to have something done (infinitive)
glossary.macket: Low German: macht; gemacht — makes; made (macken = machen, 3rd sg. and past participle; often with a particle at the end, ‘macket … up’ = macht auf)
glossary.mal: Low German: mal — once, just (the particle: ‘ik will mie mal drup bedenken’)
glossary.midde: Low German: die Mitte — middle; also ‘mit’, the particle standing at the end of mitgiewen and mitbringen (‘midde brocht’ = mitgebracht)
glossary.mie: Low German: mir — to me; also ‘mit’ where it closes a clause as the particle of mitgiewen (= mitgeben)
glossary.n: Low German: ’n = den, einen — the, a (‘an’n Disk’ = an den Tisch; ‘to’n Dörenbusk’ = zu einem Dornbusch)
glossary.nah: Low German: nach — to, towards (‘nah Hus’ = nach Haus, home)
glossary.nie: Low German: nicht — not (in this tale nie is ‘nicht’, not High German ‘nie’)
glossary.schicke: schicken — to send (1st sg. present, in the Grimms’ own gloss ‘wenn ich dich auch schicke’)
glossary.schlechte: Low German: schlecht — badly (‘et gienge ün gans schlechte’ = es ginge ihm ganz schlecht)
glossary.schöner: Low German: schöner — finer, more beautiful (comparative of schön)
glossary.schüren: Low German: scheuern — to scour, to clean (the Grimms gloss ‘Stunze schüren’ as (Gefäße reinigen))
glossary.seg: Low German: sagte — said (seggen = sagen, 3rd sg. past)
glossary.seh: Low German: sagte — said (seggen = sagen, 3rd sg. past)
glossary.sehe: Low German: sagte — said (seggen = sagen); at the tale’s end also ‘sehe’, I see (sehen, 1st sg.)
glossary.seihet: Low German: sieht, sehen — sees, see (seihen = sehen, 3rd sg. and 3rd pl.)
glossary.settet: Low German: setzt; gesetzt — sets, set themselves; set (setten = setzen, 3rd pl. and past participle)
glossary.si: Low German: sind — are (sien = sein, 1st pl.; ‘nu si wie’ = nun sind wir)
glossary.siet: Low German: sind — are (sien = sein, 3rd pl.)
glossary.sin: Low German: sein — his; also the infinitive sein, to be
glossary.sinnen: Low German: Sinnen — mind (dat. pl. of Sinn; ‘annerst to Sinnen werden’ = anderen Sinnes werden, to change one’s mind)
glossary.spannt: Low German: spannen an — harness up (anspannen; ‘spannt … an’)
glossary.stahn: Low German: gestanden, stehen — stood; to stand (stohen = stehen)
glossary.stund: Low German: stand — stood (stohen = stehen, 3rd sg. past)
glossary.te: Low German: die — the (def. art.; ‘te Tied’ = die Zeit)
glossary.ton: Low German: zum — to the, into the (to + den)
glossary.trecket: Low German: zieht — draws, puts on (antrecken = anziehen, 3rd sg.; ‘trecket … an’ = zieht … an)
glossary.vergangen: Low German: vergangen — passed, gone by (vergohen = vergehen, past participle; ‘wat vergangen was’ = was vergangen war)
glossary.vertellt: Low German: erzählt — tells; told (vertellen = erzählen, 3rd sg. and past participle)
glossary.wacker: Low German: wacker — handsome, fine, comely (of a person or a thing; not ‘brave’)
glossary.wall: Low German: der Wald — wood, forest (the Grimms gloss the dative Walle as (Wald))
glossary.was: Low German: war — was (sien = sein, 3rd sg. past)
glossary.wege: Low German: weg — away (‘wier wege west’ = wieder weg gewesen)
glossary.wer: Low German: wäre — were, would be (sien = sein, past subjunctive)
glossary.weren: Low German: werden — to become; here the passive auxiliary, to be (‘ümmebracht weren’ = umgebracht werden)
glossary.wie: Low German: wir — we; also ‘wie’, how, as
glossary.willt: Low German: wollen, wollt — want (wollen, 1st pl. and 3rd pl.)
glossary.wo: Low German: wie — how; also ‘wo’, where
glossary.wust: Low German: gewußt — known (weten = wissen, past participle)
glossary.ünnen: Low German: ihnen — them, to them (dat. pl.)
